one_liner: D command-line tools for SAM/BAM (view, flagstat, sort, markdup, index, depth) that parallelise work samtools 1.7 ran single-threaded.
what_it_does: Sambamba is a GPL command-line suite, with its BioD BAM library kept in the same tree, covering a subset of samtools: view (with a filter language and BED-driven region skipping), flagstat, index, sort (coordinate, name, samtools-style natural and Picard order), markdup (Picard's duplicate algorithm), slice, merge and depth. It is not a flag-for-flag drop-in: threads are -t instead of -@, markdup takes a coordinate-sorted BAM directly with no fixmate step, sort takes one total memory limit (-m) rather than a per-thread one, and CRAM support was removed in 0.8.0.
how_it_is_fast: Each command splits BGZF block decompression, record decoding, SAM text formatting and BGZF recompression across a D std.parallelism TaskPool. samtools 1.7 threads only the BGZF block (de)compression and formats SAM text on one thread, so its view ran at 193% CPU with -@16 in the guigolab trace. markdup is a two-pass Picard reimplementation: the first pass pairs read ends in a hash table (default 262,144 reads) with an overflow list and LZ4-compressed sorted temporary storage, collects the duplicate indices, and the second pass re-reads the BAM and rewrites the flags. sort holds as much as -m allows in RAM; per test/benchmark/stats.org, giving it 120 GB instead of 20 GB halves its own wall time because the intermediate chunk I/O goes away.
when_to_use: Marking duplicates on a coordinate-sorted BAM in one command on a many-core node, where the alternative is a samtools sort -n | fixmate -m | sort | markdup pipeline or Picard MarkDuplicates.
Converting BAM to SAM text (view) on 8-16 cores, where samtools 1.7's single-threaded text formatting is the bottleneck: 15.9 s against 77.8 s on a 4.6 GB BAM with warm caches.
flagstat on many cores: 7.7 s for sambamba 0.6.8-pre1 against 11.5 s for samtools 1.7 -@16.
Pipelines that already use sambamba's filter expressions (-F) or view -L region skipping and want its output byte-for-byte as before.
Name or coordinate sorting only when the machine has enough RAM to hold the whole file (tens of GB); this is the maintainers' own advice in issue #447.
when_not_to_use: Sorting on ordinary machines: samtools 1.7 sorted the same BAM 1.70x faster at equal 72 GB memory (146.7 s against 249.3 s), and on a Ryzen 5 3600 with a 128 MB cap sambamba 0.7.1 took 84.8 s single-threaded against 39.3 s for samtools 1.9 (33.7 s against 15.1 s with three extra threads, issue #447).
CRAM input or output: removed in 0.8.0 (only old binaries read it).

When you need current samtools/htslib features or speed: the comparison is against samtools 1.7 built with plain zlib, while htslib 1.8 added libdeflate and later samtools releases also thread markdup and use collate in place of sort -n.
When you need exact Picard duplicate counts: issue #461 shows small differences (29,370,719 against 29,393,253 duplicates), which the maintainer called not worth worrying about.
Low-core or shared nodes: the gains come from extra cores (658-1534% CPU in the trace), and index is at parity (12.7 s and 14.9 s against 13.1 s).

integration.form: CLI binary (static release builds); the BioD D library is in-tree but not packaged as a separate dub library
integration.dependencies: LDC (LLVM D compiler) to build, zlib, liblz4; meson+ninja optional (the Makefile's -singleobj LTO release build is the fastest, meson about 5% slower per INSTALL.md)
integration.min_toolchain: LDC >= 1.6.1 per README; 1.0.1 release notes say a recent msgpack was needed for recent ldc2; current builds shown with LDC 1.32 and 1.38
integration.platforms: Linux x86-64 and macOS (Conda, Homebrew, Guix, Debian packages); ARM64 builds since 0.8.0
integration.thread_safety: not documented for the library; each CLI command takes -t/--nthreads (default: all cores)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: covers view, flagstat, index, sort, markdup, merge, slice and depth with different flags (-t not -@, total -m, Picard-style markdup on coordinate-sorted input, no CRAM); samtools' other subcommands (mpileup, fixmate, collate, stats and others) are not reimplemented

gotchas: Harness flaw in guigolab/sambamBench-nf: the samtools-1.7 markdup template writes '-@{task.cpus}' without the '$' in three of its four stages. The resolved script in the report shows the literal string, the thread count never reaches samtools, and the task ran at 102% CPU against 658-890% for sambamba. The 4.49x and 3.62x markdup wins are measured against a single-threaded four-stage pipeline.

Cold-cache flaw in the same 16 CPU / 120 GB report: the tasks ran one after another, and only the first (sambamba 0.6.8-pre1 view) read the 4.59 GB BAM from disk (read_bytes 4,586,659,840; every later task read under 4 MB). Its 52.8 s and the '1.47x' view figure are therefore a cold-disk number, not a regression. The warm 0.6.6 view row (15.9 s, 4.88x) has no CPU or I/O counters in the trace, and every task ran once.

The README's 'up to 2x faster than samtools on large RAM machines (120GB+)' has no samtools measurement behind it. test/benchmark/stats.org compares sambamba with itself: sort -N took 8m0s with a 20 GB limit and 3m46s with 120 GB on a 56-core Xeon E5-2683 v3. The only same-machine comparison at 120 GB has samtools 1.7 sorting 1.70x faster.

Some older Xeons segfault under heavy hyperthreading (README, issue #335), and markdup has open crash and hang reports (#520 segfault, #519 stuck finding positions, #501 range violation). Its D garbage collector sends SIGUSR1/SIGUSR2, which gdb must be told to ignore.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Use mosdepth instead for depth or coverage (its README times sambamba depth 5.71x slower), and look at mako for template-coordinate sorting. Pick sambamba when the job is BAM duplicate marking, SAM conversion or flagstat on a many-core node and you accept GPL and an older, slower-moving codebase.
verified_claims_summary: The Guigo lab's Nextflow pipeline ran sambamba 0.6.6 and 0.6.8-pre1 (official static LDC -O3 release binaries) and samtools 1.3 and 1.7 (built with plain make, -O2, against Debian zlib, no libdeflate) on the 4.6 GB ENCODE BAM ENCFF044SJL, with 16 CPUs and 120 GB on one CRG node of unstated CPU model. Tasks ran sequentially, once each. Wall times against samtools 1.7: flagstat 7.7-11.4 s vs 11.5 s, index 12.7-14.9 s vs 13.1 s, view 15.9 s (warm) vs 77.8 s, markdup 197-245 s vs 886 s for a single-threaded pipeline, sort 249-327 s vs 147 s (samtools wins).
status_note: Stale: v1.0.1 (August 2023) is the last release and the last commits (December 2024) are build and warning fixes, with markdup crash reports still open; GPL-2.0+, with binaries in Bioconda, Debian, Guix and Homebrew, so usable as a tool but not as a permissively licensed library.
